ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2025 revised text, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3 of 2024, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identification Documents and Transaction Record Retention of Financial Institutions (PBOC Order No. 1 of 2022); Criminal Law of the PRC (Articles 191 and 312 on money laundering and proceeds of crime); Measures for the Administration of Drug Distribution Licenses of the National Medical Products Administration; SAMR Provisions on Company Registration Filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Business License) of the foreign investing parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the jurisdiction of origin; after formation of the WFOE, the SAMR local bureau issues the WFOE Business License
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Branch A for Hague Apostille member states: notarize, attach an Apostille Certificate issued by the designated Competent Authority under the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, add a certified Chinese translation, submit to SAMR or the bank. Branch B for non-member states: notarize, legalize at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin state, legalize at the Embassy or Consulate of the People's Republic of China in the origin state, add a certified Chinese translation. The two branches are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (or functional equivalent credit-information certificate) of the foreign investing parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or designated issuing authority in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Branch A for Hague Apostille member states: notarize, attach Apostille, certified Chinese translation. Branch B for non-member states: notarize, origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs legalization, PRC Embassy or Consulate legalization, certified Chinese translation. Never chain the two branches sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the foreign investing parent company authorizing incorporation of the WFOE, appointing the legal representative and first director, and granting Power of Attorney to the formation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Branch A: notarize, attach Apostille, add certified Chinese translation, submit to SAMR and the foreign-exchange bank. Branch B: notarize, legalize at the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then legalize at the PRC Embassy or Consulate, add certified Chinese translation. The two branches are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of the foreign investing parent company and the draft Articles of Association of the WFOE
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of origin for the parent document; PRC legal counsel for the WFOE draft
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Branch A: notarize and Apostille the parent Articles; the WFOE draft follows the SAMR model charter and requires no foreign authentication. Branch B: notarize and complete consular legalization for the parent Articles. The two branches are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (good standing and relationship history) of the foreign investing parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank of the parent company in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Branch A: bank-issued letter notarized and Apostilled, certified Chinese translation, direct submission to the WFOE account bank under PBOC Order No. 1 of 2022. Branch B: bank-issued letter notarized, legalized by the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalized by the PRC Embassy or Consulate, certified Chinese translation. Parallel and mutually exclusive branches; never chain sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) identification statement with passport copies and proof of address of each 25 percent plus shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of origin; passport or national identification issued by the relevant state authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Branch A: notarize identity documents and sign the UBO statement before a notary, apply for Apostille, add certified Chinese translation, file with SAMR through the Beneficial Owner Information system. Branch B: notarize, legalize at the origin-state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, legalize at the PRC Embassy or Consulate, add certified Chinese translation. Never chain the two branches sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening applies to all shareholders, directors, the legal representative, senior managers, and every identified UBO. The protocol requires (i) domestic AML CDD under the Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC (2025) and PBOC Order No. 1 of 2022, including purpose-of-account verification and source-of-funds documentation; (ii) Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) identification covering domestic, foreign, and international-organization PEPs, their family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval for any PEP relationship; (iii) continuous name matching against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK HMT Sanctions List, the FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions List, the PRC Unreliable Entity List, and the PRC Export Control Entity List; (iv) adverse-media and negative-news screening in Chinese and English; (v) sanctions-list re-screening with a 24-hour alerting SLA; and (vi) transaction screening rules for Swift LC and Bank Wire rails, including dual-use, military-end-user, and pharmaceutical-precursor diversion checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Enterprise Name Independent Declaration System integrated with the China Integrated Enterprise Registration Service Portal and the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and provincial Market Regulation Administrations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory name doctrine requires a four-tier structure in simplified Chinese ideographs: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry description plus organization form (for example: Shanghai [Trade Name] Pharmaceutical Trading Limited Liability Company). The trade name must use standardized simplified Chinese characters, shall not contain Arabic numerals or Latin letters without ministerial approval, and shall not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing enterprise name in the same industry within the same administrative division or nationally for well-known marks. A pinyin phonetic transliteration of the foreign parent name is permitted only as a supplementary trade name, never as the sole legal name. The Chinese legal name is registered in Chinese characters; the English name of the WFOE is recorded as a translation only and is not the statutory name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: China, Central, National, State (require State Council or SAMR authorization)
Bank, Insurance, Securities, Trust, Fund, Futures, Exchange, Clearing (financial license terms subject to PBOC or CBIRC approval)
Military, Armed Police, Red Cross, Red Crescent, United Nations, World Trade Organization (international and sovereign symbols)
Group, Holding, Headquarters, General Company (only upon meeting minimum capital and subsidiary-count conditions)

Hospital, Clinic, Pharmaceutical Research Institute, Vaccine, Narcotics, Psychotropic Substances, Precursor Chemicals (subject to National Medical Products Administration or Health Commission ministerial approval; vaccine and narcotic tokens are effectively blocked for private WFOEs)
Gambling, Lottery, or any token violating public order or socialist core values
Foreign-language suffixes such as Ltd., Inc., GmbH, S.A. unless the entity is genuinely foreign-invested and the suffix is declared to the registry
Tokens suggesting state sponsorship such as Examination, Supervision, Authority, Administration when used in the trade name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the autonomous name declaration is administratively rejected, the applicant should immediately file a revised name set on the same portal to avoid losing time, because a rejection does not toll the 30-day reservation window for alternative names. The applicant may then file an administrative reconsideration with the next-higher-level Market Regulation Administration within 60 days of the written rejection decision under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC, or institute administrative litigation in the competent People's Court within six months under the Administrative Litigation Law. For conflicts with existing third-party trade names or trademarks, the applicant may initiate an enterprise name dispute adjudication before SAMR or the local bureau and must concurrently reserve a fallback name. The foreign investor should instruct PRC counsel to clear the proposed trade name against Class 5 (pharmaceuticals) and Class 35 (wholesale services) of the Nice trademark classification before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this industry and business model. The Drug Distribution License (Pharmaceutical Trading License) requires a physical business premises with a lease term of at least one year, located in the same administrative district as the registered address, and subject to mandatory on-site GSP inspection by the Municipal Medical Products Administration at issuance and at renewal. The SAMR filing requires a real office address evidenced by a lease certificate or property ownership certificate. The tax authority verifies the registered address before granting general taxpayer status and may conduct an on-site inspection within the first year. Commercial banks performing Tier 2 customer due diligence under PBOC Order No. 1 of 2022 physically inspect the office before opening the corporate basic deposit account. Centralized registered-address co-working schemes in free-trade zones are accepted only for low-risk service industries and explicitly exclude pharmaceutical wholesale. Accordingly, the WFOE must secure a dedicated physical office and, where warehousing is involved, a compliant storage site before license application.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Municipal Medical Products Administration on-site GSP inspection for Drug Distribution License issuance, probability 100 percent of issuance; (2) tax bureau physical verification for general taxpayer registration, probability high, exceeding 70 percent within the first six months; (3) SAMR spot check for consistency between registered address and actual operations, probability moderate, triggered automatically by any address anomaly or complaint; (4) Public Security fire-safety inspection where API samples or dangerous-chemical goods are stored, probability high; (5) bank site visit during account opening, probability high, exceeding 80 percent; (6) PBOC sampling AML inspection once transaction volumes exceed local thresholds, probability low to moderate. Quantified aggregate risk of at least one unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months: 75 to 90 percent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: PRC Company Law (2023 Revision, effective July 1, 2024), Articles 24, 26, 32, 34, 37, 38, 40, 47 and 50; PRC Foreign Investment Law (2019), Articles 2, 6, 12 and 29; PRC Company Registration Administration Regulations (2024), Articles 5, 8 and 18.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Market Entity Registration Bureau, with delegated execution through the municipal SAMR enterprise registration halls in the jurisdiction of the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application Form for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company together with the notarized Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to an ordinary WFOE limited liability company. The registered capital is determined by the shareholders in the Articles of Association pursuant to Article 26 of the PRC Company Law and must be fully subscribed, with payment periods clearly stated. No blocked escrow account is required by national company law. For wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients, the provincial Medical Products Administration will nevertheless assess paid-up substance and operational storage capacity before issuing the Drug Distribution License. Foreign capital contributions must be remitted into a designated foreign currency capital account opened with a licensed bank and may be settled for legitimate operational use after completing foreign direct investment reporting with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 01 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] WFOE CO., LTD. The Board of Directors of [Company Name] WFOE Co., Ltd. (the 'Company') duly convened on [Date] with the required quorum present, hereby adopts the following first board resolution. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered capital of the Company shall be USD [amount] divided into [number] ordinary shares with a par value of USD [par value] per share, and that such shares shall be issued to the sole shareholder at par. The Board ratifies the subscription agreements and authorizes the Chief Financial Officer to receive capital contributions into the Company's designated foreign currency capital account in China. Contributions shall be paid in full within the period specified in the Articles of Association; no security or loan collateral may be given until full payment of the registered capital. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that [Bank] and [branch] are designated as the Company's primary bankers. The Chairperson, General Manager and Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly by any two, are authorized to open, maintain and operate bank accounts, negotiate letters of credit and documentary collections, issue payment instructions, sign SWIFT messages, and execute electronic banking agreements. Any two signatures are required for payments exceeding [threshold], consistent with the banking resolution to be filed with the bank. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be at [full address], [city], People's Republic of China, where the statutory seal, books and records will be kept; the General Manager is authorized to execute the lease and file the address certificate with the State Administration for Market Regulation. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [Name] be and is appointed Executive Director and Legal Representative; [Name] as General Manager; [Name] as Chief Financial Officer; and [Name] as Compliance Officer, each with the authorities specified in the Articles of Association and in applicable Chinese law. 5. REGULATORY AND OPERATIONAL AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the officers are authorized to apply for the pharmaceutical wholesale license, Good Supply Practice certification, import-export registration, customs code, and all environmental and fire permits required for the wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients; to engage counsel and auditors; and to take all actions necessary to implement this resolution. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all prior acts and transactions reasonably taken in connection with the formation and pre-incorporation contracts are ratified as if carried out by the Board.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investor Legalization Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal SAMR Enterprise Name Reservation System accessed through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online search for the proposed WFOE name in Chinese and English. Submit a name pre-registration application by entering the administrative division, industry term, enterprise characteristic, legal form 'limited liability company,' and desired trade name. Attach a copy of the founder's incorporation certificate, notarized foreign investor documentation, and power of attorney. After preliminary approval, a Name Reservation Notice valid for six months is generated. If the name is rejected, the applicant must log into the same portal, amend the proposal, and file anew. This check ensures there is no identical or deceptively similar trademark or enterprise name in the same industry before the formal registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name in Chinese and English
Notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation of each foreign shareholder
Foreign investor passport or legal identity document
Power of attorney signed by the foreign investor
Proposed business scope and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried for similarity or prohibited characters, promptly submit a revised name and the platform's objection statement. If the system continues to reject, request administrative reconsideration before SAMR or seek judicial review under the Administrative Litigation Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Notarization and Legalization of Founding Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal SAMR Registration Office, licensed Notary Public Office, and Chinese Embassy/Consulate or Apostille-competent authority in the foreign investor's country.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Chinese-language Articles of Association in accordance with the SAMR model charter, containing the company name, address, business scope, registered capital, shareholder contribution period, board composition, legal representative, governance rules, and dissolution clauses. Foreign investor signatures on the Articles and board appointment letters must be notarized in the investor's home country and legalized by the Chinese embassy or consulate, or apostilled if the country is a party to the Apostille Convention; all documents must then be translated into Chinese and notarized in China. The legal representative must sign the formal establishment registration application and confirm the authenticity of documents. The founder should also execute a capital contribution schedule and a bank account opening authorization, as the bank will require authenticated board minutes after registration.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Foreign investor corporate resolution and certificate of incorporation, notarized and legalized or apostilled
Appointment documents for the legal representative, directors, supervisor, and managers
Notarized lease agreement and property ownership certificate or consent letter for the registered address
Capital contribution schedule
Passport copies of proposed officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry questions the legalization or content, submit a supplemental notarial certificate or revised Articles within ten working days. If translation defects exist, retain a SAMR-accredited translation agency and re-file the corrected set.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Establishment Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Regulation Bureau (SAMR) Enterprise Registration Service Hall or the corresponding online government service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed establishment registration package with SAMR under the 'one application, one license, integrated certificates' regime. The application includes the name reservation notice, signed Articles, legal representative identity, list of shareholders, board and supervisor appointment certificates, registered address documents, and establishment application form. SAMR examines the application under commitment-based approval rules. Upon approval, SAMR issues the Unified Social Credit Code Certificate, which is the business license, and the Company acquires legal personality. The applicant must verify that the license's business scope is broad enough to include 'wholesale of pharmaceuticals, active pharmaceutical ingredients, and chemical products for pharmaceutical use' and that no foreign investment negative list restriction applies. After issuance, the license number must be used for all subsequent statutory filings.
required_dossiers: Establishment registration application form
Name pre-approval notice
Notarized Articles of Association
Identification documents for directors, supervisor, manager and legal representative
Proof of registered address, such as lease, ownership certificate, or building consent letter
Foreign investor qualification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a rectification notice, correct the nonconformity and resubmit through the same e-window within the prescribed period. If registration is denied, apply for administrative reconsideration with the superior SAMR or appeal to the people's court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Seal Carving, Tax, Social Security and Foreign Exchange Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security-approved seal engraving service, State Taxation Administration, local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange through a licensed bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the business license is obtained, arrange company seals including the company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal, invoice seal, and contract seal at a public-security licensed engraving shop. Register with the tax authority under the integrated multi-certificate system. Open a basic deposit account and a foreign currency capital account with a licensed bank. Complete foreign investment information reporting and foreign direct investment registration with SAFE through the bank. Register with social security and housing provident fund authorities. The bank will require the board resolution, business license, seals, and director identity documents. The initial registered capital contribution may be deposited into the capital account and settled for legitimate business use after the relevant declarations are recorded.
required_dossiers: Business license
Approved seal engraving registration form
Board resolution authorizing bank accounts and appointed signatories
Legal representative identity document and passport
Articles of Association
Bank account opening and anti-money laundering forms
SAFE foreign currency registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or SAFE requests additional beneficial ownership information, provide a completed ownership structure chart and source-of-funds statement. If the contribution is rejected, ensure the foreign investor's remittance reference states 'investment capital' and resubmit the corrected remittance instruction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drug Distribution License and Good Supply Practice Certification for API Wholesale
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Medical Products Administration (MPA) under the National Medical Products Administration; Municipal Ecology and Environment Bureau; local Fire and Rescue Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to commencing wholesale trading, obtain a Drug Distribution License from the provincial MPA by submitting the entity dossier, quality management system, qualifications of the licensed pharmacist serving as quality responsible person, storage facility details, information system for traceability, and the lease or property certificate of the warehouse. The MPA performs a field inspection of the warehouse to confirm temperature and humidity control, quarantine areas, cold chain equipment if applicable, security for controlled substances, and Good Supply Practice compliance. The application must also include the fire inspection acceptance certificate and the environmental registration record for warehousing if no manufacturing is conducted. The license will state the allowable pharmaceutical business scope and may impose restrictions on narcotics, psychotropics, and precursor chemicals. After issuance, the company must complete customs registration and import-export records before trading active pharmaceutical ingredients across borders.
required_dossiers: Drug Distribution License application form
Business license
GSP quality manual and standard operating procedures
Warehouse layout, HVAC qualification and temperature mapping validation report
Fire department inspection acceptance certificate
Environmental registration record or certificate
Employment contract and qualification certificate for the licensed pharmacist or quality responsible person
Traceability information system description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MPA issues a deficiency letter, respond within the official timeframe with corrective actions and revised standard operating procedures. If the license is refused, apply for administrative reconsideration at the NMPA within 60 days or bring judicial proceedings within six months.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Provincial Medical Products Administration under the National Medical Products Administration, together with the municipal market regulation bureau, local ecology and environment bureau, and Fire and Rescue Department.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Drug Distribution License (Wholesale) and Good Supply Practice (GSP) Compliance Certificate for Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Ecology and Environment (MEE) and the local municipal ecological environment bureau.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable for office-only pure trading activity. If incidental closed storage or warehousing of API drums is conducted with no chemical reaction, repackaging, or solvent handling, the facility is classified as an Environmental Registration or filing only. Any physical chemistry, formulation, repackaging, or pilot-plant activity within the warehouse will trigger a mandatory Environmental Impact Report or Form B Environmental Impact Assessment depending on hazard classification.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emission is generated by pure wholesale warehousing. Domestic sanitary wastewater must meet Integrated Wastewater Discharge Standard GB 8978-1996 Grade III when connected to municipal sewer, with COD not exceeding 500 mg/L, BOD5 not exceeding 300 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 400 mg/L, and pH in the range of 6 to 9. If refrigerated storage compressors are installed, refrigerant leakage must comply with the national ozone-depleting substances regulation. Expired, recalled, or damaged APIs and contaminated absorbents must be declared under the hazardous waste management system and must meet the leachate toxicity identification standards set out in GB 5085.7-2007.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: A Fire Safety Inspection or Check Acceptance certificate must be obtained from the local Fire and Rescue Department before storage occupancy, covering fire lanes, sprinkler coverage, loading docks, hazardous goods segregation, and emergency exits. The warehouse must also obtain a structural load verification or construction acceptance certificate for mezzanine and racking systems. Occupational workplace clearance must be secured by providing chemical safety data sheets for each API, adequate ventilation if weighing or sampling is performed, personal protective equipment, hygiene facilities, and employee training under the Work Safety Law and the Regulations on Prevention and Control of Occupational Disease.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online filing and administration portal is the National Electronic Tax Office (Electronic Tax Bureau / e-Tax system), which handles VAT, Corporate Income Tax, and export tax rebate filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the WFOE formation: Step 1: Register the wholly foreign-owned limited liability enterprise with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) under the Foreign Investment Law. Step 2: Obtain the Business License bearing the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); under the multi-license integration and multi-certificate integration reform, the USCC is the statutory taxpayer identification number (TIN) and no separate tax registration certificate is issued. Step 3: Complete post-establishment tax activation in the Electronic Tax Office, including legal representative identity verification, tax administrator confirmation, accounting system filing, and bank deposit account reporting. Step 4: Determine VAT taxpayer classification; if annual taxable sales of goods meet or exceed RMB 5 million, general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory; when below this threshold, small-scale taxpayer status applies by default but the WFOE may elect general VAT taxpayer treatment if accounting is sound. Step 5: If a foreign non-resident enterprise such as the overseas parent itself derives PRC-source income or must carry out withholding obligations, it must separately complete non-resident enterprise tax registration at the competent tax authority using its home-country registration and tax-residence evidence, after which the STA assigns a non-resident taxpayer reference code; this does not replace the WFOE's own USCC/TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: China does not offer 'check-the-box' or hybrid-mismatch entity classification; the WFOE is by law a PRC resident enterprise taxed at entity level on worldwide income under the Corporate Income Tax Law. Available elections relevant to indirect taxation are: (a) voluntary registration as a general VAT taxpayer when turnover is below RMB 5 million; (b) the optional simplified VAT collection method at 3% for specifically enumerated categories only, and generally unavailable or restricted for large API wholesale exporters; and (c) the ability to forgo small-scale taxpayer preferential treatment in order to preserve input VAT credit credibility. No statutory hybrid mismatch election exists in PRC domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the PRC Value-Added Tax Law and the current VAT implementing regulations and STA interpretations
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5 million annual taxable sales; the WFOE is a VAT taxpayer from establishment, and general VAT taxpayer registration becomes mandatory when annual taxable sales exceed this threshold; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold for wholesale API businesses with adequate accounting and invoicing capacity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China enforces real-time VAT invoice clearance through the State Taxation Administration's Golden Tax Phase IV system. The WFOE must issue invoices through the National VAT Invoice Management System or, after the digitized e-invoice reform, through the STA's fully digitalized electronic invoice service platform, where each invoice receives a unique tax-verified invoice number generated in real time and is cleared and archived in the national tax database. The system is accessed through the Electronic Tax Office or authorized e-invoice platform APIs; anti-counterfeiting is supported by the national invoice verification portal and digital invoice signature controls. For exported pharmaceutical API goods, the export declaration data from the General Administration of Customs (GACC) must be electronically matched in the STA export tax rebate system before the zero-rated refund can be claimed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The WFOE may apply the zero VAT rate and claim input VAT refund via the PRC export tax rebate scheme if: (a) the entity is the exporter of record and holds the required pharmaceutical API wholesale license and any applicable NMPA-controlled-export authorization; (b) the goods physically depart from a PRC customs port and are recorded in the GACC export declaration database; (c) the sale is made with a genuine overseas buyer, in foreign currency, and the transaction is not a sham or intra-group circular trade; (d) the export invoice, sales contract, customs declaration, transport documents, and bank receipt of payment are mutually consistent; and (e) the export tax rebate declaration is filed in the Electronic Tax Office within the statutory rebate period. For qualifying offshore digital services, zero-rating would require that the services are supplied to a non-resident, wholly consumed outside China, and have no nexus with PRC real estate or goods; a service export contract, non-resident evidence, overseas invoice, and foreign-exchange receipt proof would be required in place of customs documents.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export clearance form with Customs bill number issued by the General Administration of Customs)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing actual export
Export Sales Contract or Purchase Order with HS code, price, Incoterms, and destination port
Foreign Exchange Settlement Voucher / Bank Collection Notification / Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) proving receipt of export proceeds
Pharmaceutical API export health or sales certificate and any controlled-export permit issued by the National Medical Products Administration for the relevant API category
Electronic Export Tax Rebate Declaration / VAT export declaration populated in the Electronic Tax Office export tax rebate module
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are cross-validated by the STA against GACC customs transaction data and SAFE foreign-exchange collection data. If the input VAT refund has been paid and the claim is subsequently found false, overstated, unsupported, or if the export proceeds are not repatriated and declared within the applicable 180-day SAFE/export-verification deadline without a lawfully registered extension, the STA will require repayment of the rebated VAT plus statutory late-payment interest, and may impose an administrative penalty of up to 50 percent of the tax involved. Deliberate fraudulent export declarations with intent to obtain VAT refunds can trigger criminal liability for fraudulent export tax rebate under the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, and SAFE may impose separate foreign-exchange administrative penalties for non-repatriation or delayed reporting. The WFOE's high-risk pharmaceutical classification does not alter general VAT rules but increases document-integrity audit sensitivity; a missing FIRC, unmatched customs record, or inconsistent transport chain will result in rejection or retrospective clawback of the zero-rating benefit in the reviewed period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC), through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China operates a managed current-account convertibility regime while retaining capital-account controls. For a WFOE engaged in the wholesale distribution of active pharmaceutical ingredients, routine trade receipts and payments are current-account items and may be processed freely through designated banks provided the underlying transactions are genuine and supported by invoices, customs declarations and logistics evidence. Capital-account operations are not freely convertible: the WFOE must complete foreign direct investment (FDI) foreign exchange registration before injecting capital, open a dedicated capital account, and use the funds only for approved business purposes under the truthfulness and self-use principle before settling into RMB. There is no mandatory surrender rule for export proceeds in China; exporters may retain foreign exchange in settlement accounts or convert it at onshore bank rates. Profit remittance, however, carries procedural hurdles: an audited balance sheet and income statement, a tax payment clearance certificate, a board resolution declaring the dividend, a certified profit report, and proof that the distributions are made only from after-tax profits. Capital account inflows such as FDI equity also require registration with SAFE and verification by a Chinese certified public accountant. Overall, operational liquidity is convertible within the current-account framework, but the WFOE must maintain full SAFE reporting and documentary discipline for every cross-border flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE goods-trade administration regime, export proceeds must be received in a domestic bank through a foreign exchange settlement account or trade settlement account; there is no mandatory surrender ratio or fixed conversion ratio. For A-class trade enterprises, receipts may be retained in foreign currency indefinitely or settled into RMB at the bank spot rate by the enterprise's own decision. The statutory timeline is the contractual payment term reported in the Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System, and banks normally require export receipts to be matched to the corresponding customs export declaration before verification is closed; if the enterprise is downgraded to B/C-class, SAFE may impose an additional waiting period, often 90 days, before conversion, or require prior registration.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Account for FDI proceeds and Basic Operating Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow/Settlement Account and RMB Operating Account
Capital Account plus Trade Settlement Account for LC and collections
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: The viability of offshore fintech EMIs is low for the mainland WFOE. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Revolut and Airwallex are not licensed by the People's Bank of China or the National Financial Regulatory Administration to maintain onshore RMB accounts, open SAFE-registered capital accounts, or provide FX settlement for capital-account transactions. They can neither act as the designated bank under SAFE's FDI registration nor submit mandatory inward/outbound reporting to the State Administration of Foreign Exchange. Their role is limited to ancillary payment services in foreign jurisdictions; they cannot clear RMB through CIPS on behalf of the WFOE. Using an offshore EMI as the primary treasury channel would create an immediate KYC failure and a regulatory breach. The WFOE should rely exclusively on licensed domestic tier-1 commercial banks for all onshore account structures, while an overseas treasury satellite could use a fintech payout rail only after formal whitelisting by the group treasury and never for capital account flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch physical attendance is mandatory for the high-risk pharmaceutical WFOE, particularly for opening a capital account and activating trade settlement. SAFE-countable banks generally require the legal representative and the designated financial controller to appear in person for a KYC interview, signature verification and face-to-face confirmation. Remote consular proxy opening is not a reliable industry standard: once the offshore director provides a notarized power of attorney, some banks permit a locally authorized manager and the compliance officer to complete the interview, but they rarely allow the entire account opening to be done remotely without at least one in-person meeting. For a pharmaceutical API wholesaler, the bank may also require an on-site visit to the registered office and warehouse before the account is put into production.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity: the foreign investor is a multi-layer holding company with undisclosed natural persons and no clarity on who exercises control.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a fully documented UBO diagram showing every intermediate entity and all natural persons holding 25 per cent or more; certified passports; articles of association and certificate of incorporation from the foreign parent; apostilled or consular-legalized corporate registers; audited financial statements; source-of-wealth statements for each UBO; bank reference letters from the parent's principal bank; and a notarized declaration that no nominee shareholder exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originates from an account not held by the registered foreign shareholder, or from a jurisdiction with elevated money-laundering risk, making it impossible to verify the source of foreign funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute a board resolution approving the capital injection; provide the signed equity subscription agreement and schedule of contributions; deliver bank statements in the investing entity's name for a period of 12 months; submit the SWIFT MT103 showing remitter, recipient, amount and reference; produce the SAFE Foreign Investment Registration Certificate; obtain a CPA capital verification report immediately after each remittance; include an evidence package proving that the funds came from audited profits, internal cash resources or a disclosed external loan facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pharmaceutical wholesale risk pattern: counterparties in high-risk territories, reliance on payment pass-through entities, or unrealistic API prices that could hide trade-based money laundering or transfer mispricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a counterparty KYC file including ownership, license and sanctions status; execute sale or purchase agreements with Incoterms, unit prices and settlement terms; compile invoice-and-logistics matching sets comprising commercial invoice, bill of lading, airway bill, customs declaration and warehouse receipt; maintain documented market-benchmark pricing against recognized API price indices; provide the NMPA drug distribution license, provincial pharmaceutical trading approval and good-distribution-practice certificate; submit warehouse lease contracts, inventory reconciliation reports and a three-month cash-flow projection to demonstrate real commercial substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export control screening: payments routed through multiple intermediary banks or an end-user with potential for diversion of controlled chemical/API materials to embargoed states.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Run a documented OFAC/EU/UN/China sanctions screening report from a recognized platform; obtain end-user and end-use attestations for each bulk delivery; secure a legal opinion from licensed Chinese and international counsel confirming no sanctions nexus; apply for the Ministry of Commerce export-control license if the material is on the dual-use list; provide full supply-chain traceability including trucking and warehousing records; include enhanced due diligence packs for any counterparty in a high-risk or transshipment jurisdiction.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The WFOE must first complete SAFE FDI foreign exchange registration at the selected bank and open a dedicated foreign exchange capital account in its own name. The foreign investor then remits registered capital through SWIFT MT103 from its own bank account; the remittance must indicate the SAFE FDI registration number and use the SAFE-designated purpose code for foreign direct investment equity contributions. The bank records the incoming capital in the SAFE Capital Account Monitoring System; after receipt, the WFOE may settle the capital into RMB for permitted business use or keep it in foreign currency. Every injection must be followed by a certified public accountant capital verification report within the statutory timeframe, and the bank will conduct a post-verification check that the funded amount matches the approved registered capital schedule. No third-party pre-funding, cash deposits or account-to-account pass-throughs are acceptable for capital injection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For direct supplier payments, use SWIFT MT103 with the correct goods-trade transaction code and submit the customs declaration, commercial invoice and transport documents to the bank. For bulk pharma API purchases from overseas or high-value sales settlements, issue an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit via SWIFT MT700 through Bank of China, ICBC or China Construction Bank, or use Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) where the bank acts as principal. RMB cross-border trade payments can be cleared using CIPS through the domestic bank; USD, EUR and other currencies clear over SWIFT correspondent banking. Every disbursement must be reconciled under the SAFE goods-trade supervision system and supported by real trade documents; payments made in advance must comply with the advance-payment reporting rules, while post-shipment settlements must match the relevant export or import declarations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY forward contracts (forward settlement and sale of foreign exchange) executed onshore with a licensed domestic bank for hedging genuine trade receipts, payments and FDI proceeds expected to settle within 12 months; prohibited for speculative positions without underlying exposure.

Bilateral foreign exchange swaps with domestic banks on the basis of a real financing or current-account exposure; the swap must not exceed the maturity and notional amount of the underlying cash flow.
RMB foreign exchange options: allowable to hedge trade-linked FX risk subject to SAFE and bank product eligibility; must be backed by an actual current or capital account cash flow.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): not permitted in the onshore interbank or over-the-counter derivatives market for mainland-resident WFOEs because CNY is deliverable onshore; offshore NDFs may be considered only for offshore CNH cash-flow hedging at the holding-company level, not as the WFOE primary compliance instrument.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Annual Information Publicity Report)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each year for the immediately preceding calendar year; no national extension is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by June 30 triggers inclusion on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations. Non-rectification for three consecutive years places the WFOE on the List of Enterprises with Serious Illegal and Dishonest Acts, which can lead to administrative strike-off and revocation of the business license by SAMR. False or concealed information may additionally result in administrative fines under the Measures for Enterprise Information Publicity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce and State Administration for Market Regulation combined annual reporting system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 to June 30 of each year for the preceding calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under Article 37 of the Foreign Investment Law, failure to file or submission of false or incomplete information triggers a rectification order. If the WFOE refuses to rectify, a fine of RMB 100,000 to RMB 500,000 may be imposed, and the entity may be added to the SAMR abnormal-operations register with consequential loss of credit status and compliance standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Final Settlement and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration through the e-Tax platform and local tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Final settlement for the preceding fiscal year must be filed and settled by May 31. Quarterly prepayments are due within 15 days after the end of each quarter, and the annual payment is due by May 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpaid tax accrues daily late-payment interest at 0.05% per day. Late filing is subject to a fine of RMB 50 to RMB 2,000, increased to RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 for serious noncompliance. Understatement or evasion of corporate income tax may trigger fines of 50% to five times the amount of underpaid tax, plus possible criminal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual GSP Self-Inspection and Drug Wholesale Quality Compliance Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Medical Products Administration (NMPA regional regulator)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than March 31 for the prior calendar year; Drug Trading License renewal must be applied for within six months before the expiration of the five-year license term.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to conduct annual GSP self-inspection or maintain required audited quality records can lead to issuance of a rectification notice, suspension of the Drug Business License, administrative fines under the Drug Administration Law, and refusal of license renewal. Continued noncompliance may result in permanent closure of the API wholesale operation and strike-off of the license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Audit Report and Approval of Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of shareholders / SAMR / local tax authority dependent on filing context
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited financial statements should be approved by the shareholders within three months after year-end and retained at the registered office; the CPA audit opinion must be available for submission with the annual information report and foreign investment report by June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Lack of a certified audit opinion invalidates the WFOE's annual financial reporting and may cause the annual Enterprise Report to be rejected. Directors, supervisors, and the responsible accounting firm may be subject to fines or withdrawal of practice qualifications under the Accounting Law and Company Law if unqualified audit reports are issued or when mandatory audit is knowingly omitted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit applies to every PRC limited liability company, including a wholly foreign-owned enterprise, under Article 164 of the PRC Company Law. The audit mandate is universal and has no balance-sheet, turnover, or headcount exemption for a licensed WFOE; the quantitative threshold is effectively zero for an existing company. In addition, a pharmaceutical API wholesaler is subject to mandatory audit in every year in which it holds a Drug Business License or conducts any wholesale turnover, because the NMPA and GSP licensing regime requires certified financial statements and annual compliance reviews. Public-interest entities, financial institutions, listed companies, and large-scale state-controlled enterprises remain subject to all higher statutory audit requirements, including the applicable quantitative balance-sheet and turnover tests prescribed by the securities and financial regulators.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), substantially converged with IFRS for large and listed entities. Small-scale enterprises may apply the simplified Small Enterprise Accounting Standard, but a WFOE engaged in licensed pharmaceutical API wholesale is expected to apply full CAS where its transactions involve related parties, cross-border payments, or regulatory reporting to NMPA and tax authorities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Foreign Investment Law and the PBOC/SAMR Beneficial Ownership Information Management Measures, a WFOE must register its beneficial ownership information at incorporation and must update that information with SAMR within 30 days of any change in shareholding, control structure, or ultimate beneficial owner. There is no separate annual UBO renewal deadline; however, the annual Foreign Investment Information Report, filed between January 1 and June 30, must reconfirm the direct shareholders, ultimate controlling parties, and shareholding percentages as at December 31. Shareholding transfers that take place during the year must also be reported within the 30-day window, regardless of the annual reporting cycle.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 900 - USD 2,500 per annum for registered address, corporate secretarial services, and filing-agent support in tier-1 or tier-2 Chinese cities.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - USD 10,000 per annum for a mid-size WFOE engaged in pharmaceutical API wholesale; higher fees apply when consolidated group audits, transfer pricing documentation, or enhanced NMPA compliance reports are required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (Enterprise Income Tax Law of the PRC, Article 4)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for qualified High/New-Technology Enterprises; 100% additional super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses under Finance and Tax Announcement 2023 No. 7; preferential 15% rate for encouraged industries in the Hainan Free Trade Zone; small low-profit enterprises with adjusted taxable income not exceeding CNY 3 million effectively pay 5% until December 31, 2027.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 - Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return; filed electronically via the China Electronic Tax Administration (e-tax.chinatax.gov.cn / provincial eTax@China portal).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return plus quarterly provisional prepayment filing (Form A200000).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year-end (May 31 for calendar-year taxpayers); quarterly prepayments must be filed and paid within fifteen days after each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from principal operations (pharmaceutical API wholesale sales)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare gross sales turnover from bulk API distribution to both domestic and export customers, including invoiced Delivered Duty Paid and FOB amounts, adjusted for accrual-basis recognition; exclude VAT-output tax never recordable in revenue; reconcile to bank wires and SWIFT-letter-of-credit settlement; any invoicing through offshore intermediaries triggers transfer pricing review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of principal operations (API procurement and inventory outlay)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only properly supported costs for purchased active pharmaceutical ingredients, inbound logistics, and inventory write-downs; related-party offshore purchases must be benchmarked to comparable uncontrolled prices; customs declarations must align with CIF or FOB cost of goods sold; non-resident vendors without substance may cause recharacterization of cost base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business taxes and surcharges (including urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and real estate taxes where applicable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only taxes and levies legally borne by the WFOE; state that the enterprise income tax itself is never deductible; for cross-border transactions, any Chinese VAT or customs duties reflected in import costs must be offset only in accordance with the special VAT deduction mechanism; do not double-count foreign input taxes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses (marketing, logistics, commissions, and distribution fees)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Capitalize or expense only commercial distribution costs incurred for the WFOE; management fees or marketing support charged by the overseas parent must satisfy arm's-length standard and demonstrate actual service benefit; commissions paid to third-country intermediaries require beneficial-owner and economic-substance verification, and any undisclosed commission in ROW shipping creates customs valuation exposure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses (head-office allocations, legal, accounting, licensing, and general overhead)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow head-office sponsorship fees or management charges unless actual services were rendered and documented; permanent-establishment risk if decision-making by parent board is not locally recorded; non-resident cost allocations must be supported by contemporaneous time or activity records; otherwise add back to taxable income under EIT Law Article 41.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses (bank charges, interest on debt, and foreign exchange losses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident parent or affiliates is deductible only within thin-capitalization limits (2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for unrelated and related debt combined) and must be covered by arm's-length interest rate; the WFOE as payer must withhold 10% interest WHT unless a treaty reduces it; unpaid WHT is a nondeductible expense and becomes a leakage exposure on audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit (full absorption of Lines 1 through 6)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Show that the WFOE maintains a fully substantive distribution book: storage, quality control, insurance, and logistics; if operating profit is persistently nil or below a benchmark return while the group remains profitable, tax authorities may reallocate profit under transfer-pricing adjustments and impose deemed income on the Chinese entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total profit before taxation (operating profit plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any government grants as taxable non-operating income unless specifically designated as tax-exempt subsidies; recognize revaluation surplus from related-party shareholding transfers as taxable; verify that royalty income paid into the WFOE by the non-resident brand owner from Chinese customers is booked on gross, with appropriate VAT and CIT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after reconciliation (adding back accounting-tax differences and related-party adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for historic impairments, related-party interest additions, excess entertainment or advertising expenses, and any unverified management fee add-back; refine permanent differences for non-resident withholding taxes on dividends; for non-resident concession pricing the officer must apply the Chinese transfer-pricing adjustment clause before carrying losses forward.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax payable at 25% on taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute tax payable before foreign tax credit, deduct prepayments and tax credit for foreign withholding; the balance is payable with the annual return; if dividends are distributed to a non-resident parent immediately after audit, the board must gross-up the dividend and file withholding income tax separately using Form Non-resident Enterprise Withholding Return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under Tax Collection Administration Law (TCAL) Articles 62 and 32 include a fine of CNY 2,000 to CNY 10,000 (escalating after tax authority notification), late payment surcharge of 0.05% per day on the unpaid tax, and in serious false-declaration cases a penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid tax; criminal referral occurs under PRC Criminal Law Article 201 for intentional tax evasion whereby the taxpayer omits revenue or fabricates costs exceeding legal thresholds.
